match.reason: No existing point covers how deficits are funded by bonds and build public debt; fiscal policy is about using spending and taxes to change aggregate demand, which is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Government debt
card: When a government runs a budget deficit, it must borrow to cover the gap. It does this mainly by selling government bonds, which are promises to repay the money with interest.
Public debt is the total amount the government owes from past borrowing. Each deficit adds to it, and a surplus can be used to repay some of it.
The government pays interest to the people and institutions that hold its bonds. This interest is a cost in every future budget while the debt remains.
A larger debt can mean higher interest payments. Those payments use money that could have gone to other spending or tax cuts.
draft.remember: Deficits are funded by bonds, bonds build debt, and debt brings interest costs.

a.q: How does a government mainly fund a budget deficit?
opts: By selling government bonds to borrow money
By repaying existing public debt early
By running a surplus in the next budget
By cutting the interest it pays on bonds
a.why: A deficit means spending exceeds revenue, so the gap must be borrowed. Selling bonds does this. Repaying debt is the opposite, since it uses money rather than raising it.
a.clue: The gap needs money coming in, not going out.

b.q: A government runs deficits for several years in a row. What is the most likely effect on its future budgets?
opts: Higher interest payments take up more of its spending
Public debt falls because bonds are repaid each year
Interest costs fall because more bonds are held
Revenue rises automatically to match the larger debt
b.why: Each deficit adds to public debt, and the government pays interest on the bonds it has sold. A larger debt therefore tends to mean higher interest payments. Debt does not fall during deficits, because they add to it.
b.clue: Think about what each deficit does to the total owed.

a.best: By selling government bonds to borrow money

b.best: Higher interest payments take up more of its spending

problems.detail: "It must borrow to cover the gap" overstates the point. A deficit can also be funded by drawing down cash balances or selling assets, and HSC texts mention asset sales. The card already says "mainly by selling government bonds", so "must" should be softened, for example to "usually borrows".

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound, with one clear right answer each. The only issue is a minor overstatement in the card: a government "must" borrow to fund a deficit, when it can also use cash reserves or asset sales.
